newsitem.title: USA: NHL ICE HCOKEY-RED WINGS END 42-YEAR STANLEY CUP TITLE DROUGHT.
newsitem.headline: NHL ICE HCOKEY-RED WINGS END 42-YEAR STANLEY CUP TITLE DROUGHT.

text.p: The Red Wings beat the Philadelphia Flyers 2-1 on Saturday to complete a four-game sweep of the National Hockey League championship series and bring the Stanley Cup back to Detroit for the first time since 1955, ending the league's longest current title drought.

Nicklas Lidstrom and Darren McCarty scored for Detroit and Mike Vernon made 26 saves as the Red Wings outplayed the bigger, younger Flyers for the fourth consecutive game to set off a celebration that Detroit hockey fans have been waiting for for more than four decades.

Vernon, who was in the Detroit goal for all 16 of the team's playoff wins after being relegated to backup all season, was named winner of the Conn Smythe Award, given to the most valuable player of the playoffs.
But virtually anyone on the team could have won the Conn Smythe with the entire club playing their best hockey of the year over the final two rounds of the playoffs.
Vernon, who backstopped Calgary to the Cup in 1989, had all kinds of help from a team that played near flawless defence in front of him and put relentless pressure on the Philadelphia goalies.
The Flyers came into finals averaging better than four goals a game after dominating Pittsburgh, Buffalo and the New York Rangers in the first three rounds.
Against Detroit, they scored just two even-strength goals in the series and were held to a total of six goals in in four games.
"Detroit was on a mission. They were poised and ready," said Flyers coach Terry Murray.

The Red Wings beat St Louis, Anaheim and the defending champion Colorado Avalanche before thoroughly dominating the Flyers as Detroit's Scotty Bowman became the first coach to win the Stanley Cup with three different teams, having won previously with Montreal and Pittsburgh.
There were some tense moments in the final minute that briefly put the celebration on hold when Eric Lindros scored with just 15 seconds left, pulling the desperate Flyers within one goal.

But it was too little, too late for Philadelphia, and as Vernon steered the puck behind his net with the final seconds ticking off, Red Wings captain Steve Yzerman, who has played 14 seasons for Detroit, leaped into his goaltender's arms.
The rest of the team quickly mobbed the pair and pandemonium ensued at Joe Louis Arena.
"I don't know what to say, this is absolutely incredible," said an emotional Yzerman, the first member of the team to skate around the rink with the Stanley Cup held overhead.
"We've been close, we've been to the finals, we lost in the semifinals. We finally got here and to win at home, this is a moment you'll never get in your career ever again, it's unbelievable."
Igor Larionov, a member of Detriot's vaunted Russian Five who has won Olympic gold medals and world championships playing for the Soviet Union, was ecstatic.
"It's the happiest day of my life and I've been playing hockey for 30 years," he said.
"It's been treat for me to play on this team."
